nodes.description: Serial sural biopsies in the original family and biopsies in two subsequently reported brothers showed selective absence of large myelinated fibers with a preserved small-fiber complement. The latter brothers had no axonal degeneration in the sampled nerves; demyelination was seen only in the younger brother. This is a characteristic pathological finding, not evidence that every patient has been biopsied or that all neuropathy is uniformly demyelinating.

evidence.snippet: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease-deafness-intellectual disability syndrome is a rare demyelinating hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy characterized by early-onset, slowly progressive, distal muscular weakness and atrophy with no sensory impairment, congenital sensorineural deafness and mild intellectual disability (with absence of normal speech development).

nodes.description: In one autopsied child, large neurons were absent from dorsal root ganglia and spinal anterior horns, corresponding to the absence of large myelinated peripheral motor and sensory fibers. This supports a neuronopathic component but does not establish whether the neurons failed to develop or were lost subsequently. Faulty growth followed by axonal atrophy was proposed from serial nerve biopsies in the original sibship.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy with absence of large myelinated fibers due to absence of large neurons in dorsal root ganglia and anterior horns, clinically associated with deafness, mental retardation, and epilepsy (HMSN-ADM).
evidence.snippet: The autopsy showed complete absence of large myelinated fibers in peripheral motor and sensory nerves corresponding to a lack of large neurons in dorsal root ganglia and anterior horns of the spinal cord, moderate neurogenic muscle atrophy, and nearly complete absence of neurons in the dentate nucleus of the cerebellum.
